summary: This document defines Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation (ALPN) labels for STUN usages, such as TURN and NAT discovery. These labels let an application negotiate which STUN usage will run over a TLS connection.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 7443 defines two names that identify STUN uses during a TLS or DTLS handshake. One names TURN, and the other names NAT discovery.

questions: what are the alpn labels for stun
subtitle: Two ALPN names identify STUN usages during TLS or DTLS negotiation.

tldr.problem: When STUN runs over TLS or DTLS, the endpoints need a way to identify which STUN usage a connection will carry.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7443 defines the ALPN labels stun.turn for TURN and stun.nat-discovery for NAT discovery. A client offers supported protocols and the server selects one during the handshake.
tldr.outcome: The labels let endpoints identify these STUN usages during the TLS or DTLS handshake without adding a separate negotiation round trip.

today: RFC 7443 is an Informational document that defines ALPN labels for STUN usages. It records the labels for TURN and NAT discovery with TLS and DTLS.

sections.title: Negotiating a STUN Usage
sections.content: STUN can be transported using TLS over TCP or DTLS over UDP. Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation (ALPN) lets a client include supported application protocols in its ClientHello; the server selects one in its ServerHello. This agreement happens within the handshake.
sections.plainLanguage: The client lists the protocol names it can use during the secure handshake. The server selects one, so both sides know the connection's purpose.

sections.title: The Two Registered Labels
sections.content: RFC 7443 defines the label stun.turn for STUN used with Traversal Using Relays around NAT (TURN). It defines stun.nat-discovery for STUN used for NAT discovery. The document registers both labels for TLS and DTLS use.
sections.plainLanguage: stun.turn identifies the TURN usage. stun.nat-discovery identifies NAT discovery.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC says these ALPN identifiers introduce no specific security considerations beyond those in the ALPN extension specification. They do not affect TLS or DTLS session establishment or application data exchange.
sections.plainLanguage: The labels identify the selected STUN usage. The RFC says they do not change the security of the TLS or DTLS session.
